comment: The locked version manifest (PLAN section 04). Nothing is fetched as
'latest at install time': this file is compiled into the binary, so a
given Skrog build always installs exactly these components.
rootfs.sha256 is filled in when a rootfs release is published, copied from
the .sha256 asset the rootfs workflow attaches. While it is empty,
`skrog install` refuses and tells the user to pass --rootfs-url and
--rootfs-sha256 explicitly, rather than silently installing something
unverified. Keep these values in step with guest/rootfs/versions.env.
Older engines stay listed after a bump, with their checksums intact: they
are what `skrog engine list` offers and what `skrog engine rollback`
A published asset's filename is a fact, not text to be renamed. Every
rootfs below was published as hawser-rootfs-*, before the Skrog rename
(#1); a rename pass rewrote those filenames to skrog-rootfs-* and pointed
the manifest at assets that do not exist, which would have 404'd every
install and every rollback. Releases cut from here on are named
skrog-rootfs-*; the ones already published stay exactly as they were.
Same rule as formerRootfsHomes in internal/provision/canonical.go, and the
same reason: these describe bytes that already exist somewhere.
